Arizona Cardinals Game Day Transportation: The Ultimate Fan Guide

There's nothing quite like Arizona Cardinals game day at State Farm Stadium. The energy, the tailgates, the roar of 63,000 fans — it's an experience every football fan should have. But the parking situation? That's a different story. Here's how to make game day about football, not logistics.

The short answer: book by the hour and the vehicle is yours for the whole day. A 6-hour game day is $750 before tax on a Luxury SUV (6 seats, $125/hr), $870 on an Executive Sprinter (14 seats, $145/hr), or $1,500 on a Party Bus (28 Pax) — about $54 per person with 28 aboard. Drinking on the ride is legal for passengers 21+ under A.R.S. § 4-251 (details in the FAQ).

State Farm Stadium: The Basics

Location & Capacity

  • Address: 1 Cardinals Drive, Glendale, AZ 85305
  • Capacity: roughly 63,000 for football
  • Surface: Natural grass (retractable field)
  • Roof: Retractable — games are climate-controlled

Getting There

  • From Phoenix: I-10 to Loop 101
  • From Scottsdale: Loop 101 west
  • From Tempe: I-10 west to Loop 101

The Parking Challenge

State Farm Stadium has massive parking infrastructure:

  • General and premium lots, all paid
  • Lots open hours before kickoff
  • Post-game exit time: 45-90 minutes

The problem isn't availability — it's the experience. Searching for spots, walking a half-mile in the heat, then sitting in post-game gridlock for an hour.

Cardinals Transportation FAQ

Q: Can we bring our tailgate gear?
A: Yes. Sprinters have real cargo space for coolers and chairs; luggage and gear fit is confirmed separately when you book.

Q: Where exactly do you pick up after the game?
A: We'll provide a specific meeting point before the game. It's typically a 5-10 minute walk from your section.

Q: What if the game goes to overtime?
A: We stay until you're ready. Extra time is simply billed at your hourly rate.

Q: Can we drink in the vehicle?
A: Yes, if you're 21 or older. Arizona's open-container law (A.R.S. § 4-251) exempts passengers in a vehicle for hire such as a party bus or limousine, so alcohol is legal on board. It's BYOB, nobody under 21 drinks, and the driver never does — read the full explainer.

Q: How do you handle group pickups from different areas?
A: We designate a meeting point. Everyone walks there, we load up together.

Q: What's the cancellation policy?
A: Cancellation terms depend on your date and booking; read the cancellation policy before you book. One free date change at 72+ hours. See our policies page.
